seed: Objects of type `reflection` under action ACTION4 with touching neighbours [player,wall,wall] show mixed outcomes: h,pixels,y x1, h,pixels,w,x,y x1. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: a global object such as a counter, HUD element or legend, read as state. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Two-axis mirror puzzle on 21x21 grid of 3x3 blocks: H-axis row, V-axis col, 2 pieces, target blocks; selection read from 0 hole centres.
ACTION5 cycles H->V->pieces(by min block)->H; A1/A2 move H or piece by a block row, A3/A4 move V or piece by a block col (pieces blocked by bounds/other pieces).
Pieces reflect across V (visible gray), across H and H+V (invisible occluders); per-block layer stacks P>R>I>T>W, ring=top sprite, centre=first solid else top fill; re-extract 4-conn comps, wall/player names ranked with foreign 0 dots, targets merged at bbox gap<=4.
Hypothesis (counter decides reflection A4 outcome) refuted: counter never changes; mixed outcomes are just reflections re-rendered/re-ranked as V moves.
Unconfirmed: ACTION6/7 (treated as no-op), piece cycle order beyond first, merged-piece splitting (pieces never touched). Stateless; passes without hidden state.
